correctness.rationale: Independent proof reconstruction of RESULT.md: one replacement changes overlap with the target by at most one, and successive replacements reach it in r minus the overlap. The normalized order guarantees disjoint pairs, so diameter equals normalized rank and distinguishes unequal ranks. A fixed-distance test has two free endpoints and reuses a third name for its recursively scoped helpers. At each move, first restrict the cell matching to the retained sets (merge the old patterns that now coincide, and discard the all-zero cell). Their union uses at most (p−1)r points. Both ground sets have at least r fresh points when their orders are at least pr, so a response can match exactly the number selected from every cell and from outside the union. The matched profiles preserve equality and adjacency, indefinitely, including repeated pebbled vertices. For each 2r<t≤pr write t=jr+i with 1≤i≤r and 2≤j≤p−1. Witnesses consisting of j pairwise disjoint bases and one r-set disjoint from all but the first, meeting the first in r−i points, exist exactly at orders at least t. Each distance test locally shadows an unused endpoint name from the j+1 outer names. Applying t=n+1 separates every smaller order n<pr from every larger one. This gives the count and minimum representative within the family. The least-width claim is restricted to 3r≤n<m; the game works at width 3 as well and hence rules out all smaller widths there. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and the bundled logic/Venn source and output pairs: pair refinement corroborates width 3, while higher-width samples check the stronger cell-profile invariant, not a general FO^p enumeration. The proof, not those outputs, establishes the unrestricted claim.

value.rationale: For a natural family of uniform-matroid basis graphs, the result specifies exactly what a fixed number of reusable variables can recover even with unlimited depth. Both the threshold and the intervening order distinctions matter: an eventual equivalence bound alone would not identify the least width or the smallest Johnson representative. The construction gives an explicit unbounded hierarchy at a fixed rank without invoking counting, and does not assert minimum representatives in arbitrary graph families.
